claim: TRIBE v2 beat an optimized deep-linear FIR baseline on every dataset
quote: Across all datasets, TRIBE v2 significantly outperforming the optimized linear baseline

claim: The Deep FIR baseline was built on the same embeddings so the gap isolates architecture
quote: This ensures that the performance gap reflects the architectural advantage of our transformer-based integration rather than differences in input features or optimization scale.

claim: Encoding accuracy scales log-linearly with data volume, no plateau
quote: We observe a log-linear increase in encoding accuracy across the Courtois NeuroMod dataset without any plateau

claim: Zero-shot predictions estimate the group response better than most individual recordings
quote: TRIBE v2’s predictions provide a more accurate estimation of the group response than the recording of most individual subjects

claim: On HCP, Rgroup near 0.4, two-fold over median subject
quote: a two-fold improvement over the median subject’s group-predictivity

claim: HCP gap largest because best SNR: only 7T, most stimulus repetitions
quote: which features the best signal-to-noise ratio (it is the only dataset recorded with a 7T scanner, and features the most repetitions of each stimulus)

claim: Finetuning one epoch on half a subject's data gives 2-4x over per-subject linear encoder
quote: leads to a two- to four-fold improvement over a linear encoder trained from scratch on each subject

claim: In-silico flashed images produce ventral-stream activity peaking at 5s
quote: activity increases in the ventral visual stream, and peaks 5 seconds after the stimulus onset, as expected from the hemodynamical delay

claim: Visual localizers recover FFA/PPA/EBA/VWFA
quote: the fusiform face area (FFA) for faces, the parahippocampal place area (PPA) for places, the extrastriate body area (EBA) for bodies and the visual word-form area (VWFA) for written characters

claim: Sentence response starts t=3s in primary auditory cortex, propagates to language network
quote: the elicited response begins at t=3 seconds in the primary auditory cortex then propagates to the whole language network

claim: Emotional vs physical pain recovers TPJ and MTG
quote: TRIBE v2 correctly recovers two important regions: the temporo-parietal junction (TPJ) and the middle temporal gyrus (MTG)

claim: Both linguistic contrasts show left lateralization; semantic for sentences-vs-wordlists, syntactic for complex-vs-simple
quote: TRIBE v2 correctly predicts a higher lateralization to the left hemisphere, as well as higher responses in semantic regions (e.g. TPJ) for the former and syntactic regions (e.g. Broca) for the latter

claim: Top five ICA components resemble five known functional networks
quote: the primary auditory cortex, the language network, the motion detection area, the default mode network and the visual system

claim: Unimodal ranking: text lowest, then audio, then video
quote: text achieves the lowest average encoding score overall, followed by audio, then video

claim: Text dominates language cortices and much of prefrontal lobe
quote: dominates in the language processing cortices but also in large parts of the prefrontal lobe

claim: Largest multimodal gains at temporal-parietal-occipital junction, up to 50%
quote: the largest gains are around the temporal-parietal-occipital junction (with up to 50% increase in encoding score), and to a lesser degree in the prefrontal cortex

claim: Subcortical scores more uniform, 2-3x lower, still significant in most areas
quote: which tend to be more uniform and lower by two to three folds, but remain significant in most areas

claim: Modality dropout zeroes a modality with p=0.3, at least one left
quote: we introduce modality dropout: during training, we randomly mask off each modality by zeroing out the corresponding input tensor with a probability p = 0.3, resampling such that at least one modality is left unmasked

claim: Subject dropout enables zero-shot group prediction
quote: This forces the model to maintain accurate predictions even without information on the subject, and enables our model to be used to predict group responses in a zero-shot manner.

claim: Averaging video patch tokens discards positional info, expected to hurt retinotopic areas
quote: it comes at the cost of discarding positional information, which we expect to deteriorate encoding performance in low-level visual areas which exhibit a retinotopic mapping

claim: Most fundamental limitation: brain modelled as passive observer, not an agent
quote: the model currently treats the brain as a passive observer of naturalistic stimuli; it does not yet model the brain as an active agent producing behavior

claim: One TR kept every 60s to ensure sample independence given fMRI autocorrelation
quote: Given the autocorrelation inherent to fMRI signals, we only keep one TR every 60 seconds to ensure the independence of the samples.

claim: Corpus is over 1,000 hours of fMRI across 720 subjects
quote: Leveraging a unified dataset of over 1,000 hours of fMRI across 720 subjects

claim: Audio embeddings are bidirectional; text and video only carry the past
quote: the resulting embeddings carry bidirectional information about both the past and future of the stimulus window, whereas text and video embeddings only contain information about the past

claim: Earlier iteration won Algonauts 2025, first of 263 teams
quote: an earlier iteration of our TRIBE v2 architecture achieved first place out of 263 teams
